blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it
R-ops-1 (Payment call has no timeout and can hang checkout forever) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it
R-ops-2 (Unbounded retry loop with a fixed 1 s sleep, also on non-retryable errors) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it
R-ops-3 (Retrying a non-idempotent charge POST without an idempotency key can charge an order twice) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it
R-ops-4 (Payment failures are swallowed without any log) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.recommendation: Pass an explicit `timeout=` (connect and read) to `requests.post`, so that a provider that accepts the connection but never answers raises `requests.Timeout` instead of blocking the checkout worker indefinitely; handle that timeout as an outcome of unknown state (see R-ops-3).
findings.title: Payment call has no timeout and can hang checkout forever

findings.recommendation: Bound the retries (a small maximum attempt count or total deadline), space them with exponential backoff and jitter, retry only transient failures (connection errors, timeouts, 429/5xx) and raise immediately on 4xx such as a declined card or a bad request, then raise an actionable error once retries are exhausted.
findings.title: Unbounded retry loop with a fixed 1 s sleep, also on non-retryable errors

findings.recommendation: Send an idempotency key derived from the order (e.g. an `Idempotency-Key` header built from `order_id`, if the provider supports it) on every attempt so the provider deduplicates retries; without one, do not retry after a request may have reached the provider (read timeout, 5xx, connection reset after send) — surface it as an unknown-state failure to reconcile instead.
findings.title: Retrying a non-idempotent charge POST without an idempotency key can charge an order twice

findings.recommendation: Log each failed attempt with structured fields (order_id, attempt, HTTP status or exception class, provider request id when present — never card data or credentials), and raise an error naming the order and the last cause when giving up, so an operator can see and act on payment failures.
findings.title: Payment failures are swallowed without any log

findings.recommendation: Read the provider endpoint from the environment or the project configuration (e.g. `PAYMENT_URL` env var), so staging and tests can target the provider's sandbox and an operator can repoint it without a release.
findings.title: Production payment URL hard-coded instead of read from configuration
